evacuation.title: Evacuation levels
evacuation.intro: Oregon uses three statewide evacuation levels. Know what each level means and what to do — levels are set by local officials and shown on official county and state maps.

1.name: BE READY
1.description: Be aware of danger in the area. Stay informed… This is the time to pack and prepare to leave.

2.name: BE SET
2.description: There is significant danger in the area. Be prepared to leave at a moment's notice… Leave if you feel unsafe. You don't need to wait for another evacuation notice.

3.name: GO NOW!
3.description: Leave immediately! There is extreme danger in the area… Do not return to the area until officials announce the area is safe.

countyFinder.title: Find your county's evacuation and alert links
countyFinder.intro: Evacuation status is set county by county. Sign up for your county's official emergency alerts and check its evacuation page during an incident.

relief.title: Relief & assistance
relief.intro: Official and nonprofit resources for shelter, financial help, and fire information. Every entry is sourced and carries a review date.

211info.description: Oregon's community resource directory — shelter and resource questions during wildfires. Language interpreters available.

red-cross-region.description: Cascades Region page with local disaster response, volunteer, and donation information.

red-cross-shelter-finder.description: Map of open Red Cross shelters — the same shelter source the FEMA app uses.

oregon-oem.description: State emergency management — disaster assistance programs, including Individual Assistance after federal declarations.

oregon-wildfire-portal.description: The state's official wildfire portal: evacuation levels, preparedness, and current response.

fema-disaster-assistance.description: Apply for federal assistance and upload documents after a presidential disaster declaration.
